original_source_text: Co-designing chiplet-based neural-network accelerators spans partitioning, placement, dataflow, and microarchitecture under tight energy and latency limits. Fast system-level estimators scale to large searches but blur intra-core effects that dominate energy; fine-grain reference models capture them but are too slow in-loop. We close this speed–fidelity gap with a coarse-to-fine flow: a compact, architecture-aware surrogate of intra-core cost guides the global search, and only top designs are rechecked with the reference model. Our contributions are an energy-focused feature space and a lightweight predictor across convolutional and GEMM-like workloads. On ResNet-50 and a Transformer, we reduce a manufacturing-weighted energy–delay objective by up to 62\% and 44\%, respectively.
